text: Still working on it. The bug is in the Unwrap method of gin.Error: it is declared on the pointer receiver, so errors.Is()/errors.As()/errors.Unwrap() do not see the wrapped error when a gin.Error value (rather than *gin.Error) is used, contradicting the method's documented contract. Fix: declare Unwrap on the value receiver. ETA ~6 min to fix and verify.
Still investigating. I have narrowed it to the status-code handling in response_writer.go (WriteHeader/WriteHeaderNow/Status) and am verifying against the documented behavior. ETA ~10 min.

Fix applied: Unwrap is now declared on the value receiver of gin.Error, so errors.Is/errors.As/errors.Unwrap see the wrapped error for both Error and *Error values. Running the full suite to confirm nothing regressed.

Still hunting. The status-code logic in WriteHeader/WriteHeaderNow/Status looks correct for the cases the existing tests cover, so the fault must be in an uncovered path (post-write WriteHeader / WriteString). ETA ~6 min.
Still hunting the params bug in tree.go. ETA ~6 min.

Fix applied in tree.go: findCaseInsensitivePathRec followed the first child when the node had a wildcard child, which panics with "invalid node type" (and returns a wrong path) as soon as a node has several children plus a wildcard. It now follows the wildcard child, which is always the last one. Verifying now.

Fix applied in context.go: the NegotiateFormat comparison loop lacked the `i < len(offer)` bound, so it indexes offer out of range (panic) whenever an offered type is shorter than the accepted type. Fixed. Verifying now.
Looking at it now: attachment filename escaping in context.go (FileAttachment/escapeQuotes). ETA ~5 min.
Fixed and verified: gin.Error.Unwrap now uses a value receiver, so errors.Is/errors.As/errors.Unwrap work for both Error and *Error values. Full test suite still green.

Fixed and verified: findCaseInsensitivePathRec followed children[0] when a node had a wildcard child, so with several children plus a wildcard it panicked with "invalid node type" (or returned a wrong path). It now follows the wildcard child, which is always the last one (same rule as getValue). Full suite green.

Fixed and verified: the NegotiateFormat comparison loop lacked the `i < len(offer)` bound, so it indexed `offer` out of range (panic) whenever an offered media type was shorter than an accepted one. Bound added. Full suite green.

Fixed and verified: FileAttachment put the filename into the Content-Disposition header unescaped, so a filename containing a double quote (or backslash) produced a malformed header. Added escapeQuotes (quoteEscaper replacer) in utils.go and used it for the ASCII branch. Full suite green.

Not fixed yet. I verified the covered paths of WriteHeader/WriteHeaderNow/Status/Written/Size/reset/Flush/Hijack behave correctly, so the fault is in an uncovered path (post-write WriteHeader, WriteString, or the zero-value writer); I'm still narrowing it down.

Not fixed yet. getValue's param saving and the skippedNode rollback look correct for every case the existing tests cover, so I'm still hunting the specific route/request combination that yields empty params.

Session time is up; I could not pin down the exact fault in response_writer.go. All paths I could exercise (WriteHeader before/after write, WriteHeader(0)/(-1), WriteHeaderNow, Write, WriteString, Status, Size, Written, reset, Flush, Hijack) match the documented behaviour, so I left the file untouched rather than risk breaking existing green tests.

Session time is up; I could not pin down the empty-params case in tree.go. getValue's param saving and the skippedNode rollback are correct for every case the existing tests cover, so I left that code untouched rather than risk breaking existing green tests.
